399:         let mut shared = self.inner.shared.lock();

524:                 shared = self.shared.lock();
525:             }
526: 
527:             // IDLE
528:             self.metrics.inc_num_idle_threads();
529: 
530:             while !shared.shutdown {

532: 
533:                 shared = lock_result.0;
534:                 let timeout_result = lock_result.1;
535: 
536:                 if shared.num_notify != 0 {

538:                     // acknowledge it by decrementing the counter
539:                     // and transition to the BUSY state.

541:                     break;
542:                 }
543: 
544:                 // Even if the condvar "timed out", if the pool is entering the

546:                 if !shared.shutdown && timeout_result.timed_out() {

551:                     join_on_thread = std::mem::replace(&mut shared.last_exiting_thread, my_handle);

559:             if shared.shutdown {

part.text:
Fixed. Summary:

- `tokio/src/runtime/scheduler/multi_thread/handle/metrics.rs:12` — `num_blocking_threads()` now returns `blocking_spawner.num_threads().saturating_sub(self.num_workers())`, since worker threads are spawned via `spawn_blocking` (worker.rs:447) and were being double-counted.
- Applied the identical fix to `tokio/src/runtime/scheduler/multi_thread_alt/handle/metrics.rs:10`.

Validation: `cargo test -p tokio --all-features --test rt_metrics` with `RUSTFLAGS="--cfg tokio_unstable"` — `num_blocking_threads` passes (plus 19 other metrics tests; only the two network-dependent `io_driver_*` tests fail due to the container lacking bindable addresses, unrelated to this change).
